subject: Hosted API: sudden tail latency + error spike impacting Beacon Health
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@beaconhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexplained latency spike causing failed patient-facing requests

Jonas —

We started seeing a sharp increase in perceived latency and 5xx errors from Redwood's hosted API hitting our production workflows since ~08:45 PST this morning. Some quick numbers from our side: p50 ~130ms (normal), p95 jumped to ~2.1s (was ~160ms), p99 ~4.3s. Error rate is ~5% for request ids prefixed with beac- at 08:46–09:05. This is causing timeouts in our intake pipeline and a handful of patient-facing forms to retry repeatedly.

Example request ids: beac-298172, beac-298173, beac-298180.

We need immediate assistance — can you confirm if there are platform-side regressions or ongoing maintenance? We're escalating internally if this continues. Attaching a screenshot of our dashboard showing the spike.

Elena
Elena Ruiz
Site Reliability Engineer, Beacon Health
attachments: beacon-prod-latency.png
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@beaconhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Aug 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexplained latency spike causing failed patient-facing requests

Elena — thanks for the rapid heads up and the sample request ids. We see the same signal on our side and are treating this as Sev2-P1 for Beacon.

Immediate steps I'm kicking off now:
- Opened a live investigation with infra/serving (cc'd).
- Temporarily routing a subset of your traffic to rdx-3-small-quant (lower memory, smaller batch footprint) to reduce tail latency while we debug.
- Narrowing batch window to 12ms and increasing per-worker concurrency by 25% as a quick mitigant.

Can you confirm whether any change on your side coincided with the start time (traffic pattern, payload size, new model prompts)? If not, we will proceed and keep you updated every 30 minutes.

Next update in 30m or sooner if we have a root cause.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Aug 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Unexplained latency spike causing failed patient-facing requests

Jonas / Dylan — quick diagnostic notes from the serving team after an initial triage:

What we're seeing
- Worker-local request queue depth for the Beacon tenant climbed from median ~40 to sustained ~800 at peak on the affected pool between 08:40–09:15.
- Large, late-forming batches created by a recent batching-path change (runtime v2027.07.30) are amplifying per-request CPU and serialization overhead.
- A higher-than-normal rate of KV-cache misses for prefix caching increased effective token decoding work per request (cold-cache penalty).

Probable proximate cause
- The autoscaler tuning that lowered min_workers for cost optimization inadvertently reduced headroom during a burst, allowing queue depth to accumulate and triggering bigger batch formation. The batching-path change we merged in v2027.07.30 exacerbated the effect by waiting slightly longer for batch fill under specific arrival patterns.

Immediate mitigations applied (already rolling)
- Pinned Beacon to rdx-3-small-quant variant (less batch amplification).
- Reduced batch window from 25ms -> 12ms for the impacted pool.
- Increased min_workers by 2x for the pool; manually scaled additional workers to drain backlog.
- Forced warm prefix-cache for top prompt prefixes seen in their traffic.

Next steps (48h plan)
- Roll back the batching-path change for the affected runtime on the pool and validate with controlled traffic.
- Restore autoscaler min_workers with a safety margin and add an emergency scale trigger.
- RCA doc and postmortem (ops_snapshot_20270801.log attached).

I'm sending a short status note to Beacon once we confirm backlog draining.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
SRE, Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference

2) Schedule a 30-min post-incident bridge for today at 15:30 PST for a quick sync on rollback timing and customer communication.

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Aug 2027 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Update & mitigations applied — Beacon Health incident (08/01)

Elena — follow-up after the immediate mitigations we rolled earlier today. TL;DR: backlog fully drained; tail latency and error rate returned to baseline during the 12:30–14:00 PDT window on 8/1 after the mitigations below.

What we did (summary)
- Temporarily routed ~40% of Beacon traffic to rdx-3-small-quant to reduce batch amplification.
- Reduced global batch window for the pool to 12ms and increased min_workers by 2x; manually added warm workers to accelerate drain.
- Warm prefix cache populated for top request patterns.

Status & next steps
- Current metrics: p95 ~170ms, p99 ~360ms, error rate <0.2% for the past 24h.
- We will roll back the batching-path change for the runtime on the affected pool by 08/04 10:00 PDT behind a canary and verify with synthetic traffic.
- RCA & postmortem (follow-up doc, HB-4921) will be shared within 72 hours.

Links: https://dash.redwoodinference.com/instances/beacon-prod?range=1h
Attachments: temporary-routing-config.json

Please let me know if you need anything else or want a short handoff call. We appreciate your patience and will keep you informed as we complete the RCA.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
